author: NorthEast News Desk
body: NASA astronaut and Brown University alumna Jessica Meir spoke remotely with about 75 Brown students and faculty members from the International Space Station before the start of fall classes, the university said Friday. The private session lasted about an hour and included a tour of the station's Cupola observation module.

Meir described her path to becoming an astronaut and life aboard a laboratory orbiting roughly 250 miles above Earth at about 17,000 miles per hour. Brown planetary scientist Jim Head facilitated the conversation. NASA required specific details to remain private because the event was part of behavioral-health support provided to astronauts on long missions.

Meir graduated from Brown in 1999 and joined NASA's astronaut corps in 2013. During her first mission in 2019, she and Christina Koch completed the first all-woman spacewalk. Meir now commands SpaceX Crew-12, which arrived at the station earlier in 2026 and is expected to return late this year. For students in Providence, the call offered a direct view of scientific work in orbit and a rare chance to ask questions of an alumna leading a current space mission.
dek: The Brown alumna connected with about 75 students and faculty from the International Space Station and gave a guided tour of the orbiting laboratory.
headline: Astronaut Jessica Meir speaks with Brown students from space
